# Release artifact ownership

Canonical sources are TypeScript, skills, neutral agents, docs, hooks and adapter bindings. `npm run build` rebuilds the CLI, library, review entry/declarations, review schemas and both complete native packages. It replaces `bin/` and `dist/` so removed modules and resources cannot survive an earlier build. The executable CLI shim is generated by `scripts/build.mjs`.

| Canonical source | Generated output |
| --- | --- |
| `src/` and root package metadata | `bin/`, library and review bundles/declarations, review JSON schemas |
| `agents/` and host bindings | Native Claude Markdown and Codex TOML registrations |
| Skills, docs and hooks | Complete host trees under `dist/claude` and `dist/codex`; Codex omits Claude hooks |
| `adapters/plugin.json` and package version | Native manifests in both host trees |
| `adapters/claude/marketplace.json` | `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
| `adapters/codex/marketplace.json` | `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` |

Source PRs commit canonical changes. Build and test locally, then omit generated paths from the commit. CI rejects added/modified generated files, including hidden catalogs; deletions are allowed for explicit migrations. Release outputs remain tracked for native Git marketplace installation. Gitignore therefore does not hide changes to already tracked output after a rebuild. `npm run check:source-status` ignores generated changes and fails if any canonical changes remain uncommitted, including untracked files.

The ownership migration keeps the previous committed Claude catalog and output working until release preparation. It does not remove all distributed artifacts in a source PR. During preparation, `scripts/set-version.mjs` updates package/lock metadata and existing native manifests; the build derives all new manifest versions from the package. Catalogs have no version field. Once both native trees are complete, the build generates the catalogs and removes the legacy root plugin manifest. The Git release plugin commits catalogs, native trees, library/CLI outputs, schemas and stale deletions together. The Claude source becomes `./dist/claude` in that same release commit. npm publication includes the root/review exports, both native trees and both catalogs.

Run `npm run test:release:artifacts` to exercise that preparation against a disposable local Git remote. It proves ignored dotfiles and every generated file enter the release commit, stale files disappear, unrelated sources stay out, catalogs switch atomically, versions match, and the extracted npm artifact runs all three relocated CLIs and imports the root/review/schema APIs. It never publishes to a registry or pushes over the network. CI runs it too.

After a release containing the new native target is published, existing Claude installations can refresh the marketplace and reinstall to discard the old root layout. Use the original installation scope; this example is user scope and preserves plugin data:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace update flight-rules
claude plugin uninstall flight-rules@flight-rules --scope user --keep-data
claude plugin install flight-rules@flight-rules --scope user
```

Restart the session after reinstalling. No installation changes are performed by the artifact checks. Codex native parser/catalog validation uses `npm run test:agents:codex-config`; installing the Codex plugin does not register its standalone project agents or put the CLI on PATH. E4/E5 own runtime permissions, project setup and complete workflow execution evidence.
